# Writing style

Rules for user-facing text in the product: UI copy, errors, empty states,
notices, `aria-label`s, and emails. Marketing pages share the voice but have
their own rules for headings.

Follow this doc, not the strings around your change: much existing copy
predates it. When editing a file that breaks these rules, fix only the text you
touch. Command names, code, and third-party names keep their own spelling
(`entire login`).

## Voice

Plain, specific, calm. Say what happened and what the reader can do next.
Address the reader as "you". Use "we" when Entire is doing something
(`We’re checking your GitHub setup.`), and "Entire" when naming the product.

## Rules

**Use sentence case** for headings, buttons, labels, titles, and menu items.
Only blog and changelog post titles use title case.

| Do                  | Don’t               |
| ------------------- | ------------------- |
| `Save changes`      | `Save Changes`      |
| `Page not found`    | `Page Not Found`    |
| `Delete repository` | `Delete Repository` |

**End sentences with a period. Leave it off everything else**: headings,
buttons, labels, badges, empty states, and short confirmations.

| Do                                            | Don’t                                        |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `No approvals yet`                            | `No approvals yet.`                          |
| `Anyone with the link can view this session.` | `Anyone with the link can view this session` |

**Write errors as "Couldn’t" + what failed + the next step**, without "We".
Give the cause when you know it. After a colon, start lowercase unless the
rest is a message passed through from the server.

| Do                                             | Don’t                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `Couldn’t save the secret. Try again.`         | `Failed to save secret`                 |
| `Couldn’t add Asia Pacific: Region is full.`   | `Oops! Something went wrong.`           |
| `Couldn’t load branches. Close and try again.` | `Error loading branches. Please retry.` |

**Write empty states as "No" + the thing**, with "yet" when it can still
appear.

| Do                   | Don’t                               |

412	      let token: string | undefined
413	      do {

436	        for (const commit of page.commits ?? []) {

438	          for (const match of (commit.message ?? "").matchAll(/^Entire-Checkpoint:\s*(\S+)/gm))

444	        checkSize()

449	      } while (token)

473	          // a cursor. At the cap completeness is unknown; never silently truncate.
474	          if (previews.length >= 1000)
475	            throw new MemoryReadError(503, "Trail checkpoint membership reached the batch limit")
476	          for (const checkpoint of previews) {
477	            if (checkpoint.checkpointId) checkpoints.add(checkpoint.checkpointId)
478	            for (const session of checkpoint.sessions ?? [])
479	              if (session.sessionId) sessions.add(session.sessionId)
480	          }
481	        }

483	      }
484	    }

486	      return EMPTY_MEMORIES
487	    const membership = {

489	      checkpointIds: [...checkpoints],
490	      sessionIds: [...sessions],
491	      trailIds,
492	      pageSize: opts.pageSize ?? 50,
493	    }
494	    // The UI requests one complete read: resolve membership once and reuse it
495	    // for every fact page under the same viewer identity.

## Why

Customer report (COR-2291): six memories synced successfully to the hosted memory set, but the repo Memories page showed "No memories yet". The fix is to split the logic — the list path should use whole-memory visibility semantics with a new blank-commit case, while the facets path retains the original per-row rule based on trailId, unanchored status, or commit-on-default. I'll keep the list visibility test unchanged, remove the duplicated comment I introduced at brainstore.test.ts lines 607-609, and leave the facets viewerState logic as-is since it still derives repoHasFacts from raw items.

input.description:
Follow-up to COR-2291 (trail https://entire.com/gh/entirehq/-/trails/22893).

The Memories list now shows memories whose provenance has no commit anchors (session/checkpoint/turn-only). Facets cannot adopt the same rule: `MemoryFacetCandidates` returns DISTINCT (author, trail_id, commit, unanchored) rows, and a blank-commit row cannot prove the whole memory is commit-less — a memory with a session anchor plus an off-default commit anchor also emits a blank row, so admitting blank rows would leak filter choices for list-hidden memories.

The BFF therefore keeps facet rows on the conservative per-row rule, which under-includes: session/checkpoint-only memories appear in the list but their authors are missing from the author filter, and `hasNoTrail` can stay false while visible no-trail memories exist.

Fix: have the candidate query report whole-memory commit presence (e.g. a `hasCommitAnchors` column per row, or collapse candidates per fact), then update the BFF's `facetCandidateVisible` to match the list's `repositoryMemoryVisible`.
